newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albanians loot weapons as unrest moves north.
newsitem.headline: Albanians loot weapons as unrest moves north.

text.p: An angry crowd of about 100 Albanians denouncing President Sali Berisha invaded a military base near the southern town of Elbasan on Wednesday and looted its stock of rifles and ammunition.
The incident marked the furthest advance north of the unrest that has swept most of southern Albania since the collapse of fraudulent pyramid schemes in which thousands had invested their savings.
Members of the Shik secret police in black leather jackets and uniformed police officers fired in the air in an attempt to frighten the crowd, which ran out of the back of the base.
One of the looters was shot in the leg, but this was almost certainly an accident, given the number of small boys brandishing automatic weapons in the base.
The base is located at the village of Mjeks, a short distance south of Elbasan, itself just 55 kms (34 miles) from the capital, Tirana. Elbasan was quiet immediately after the incident.

Soldiers unlocked the gates and stood by as local people, including young boys and men in their 80s, moved into the base and made off with as many as five rifles slung over their shoulders and with pistols and ammunition magazines stuffed into their pockets.
"Down with Berisha," shouted one young man, while others said they wanted the government to pay back the money they had lost in the pyramid schemes.
"I am doing nothing," said a soldier standing outside the guard house in warm spring sunshine while young men carried off rifles and pistols.
The only weapons left behind in the arsenal were seven heavy machine guns too bulky to carry. Pistols, rifles and ammunition belts dropped by the looters littered the parade ground.
Will, a 29-year-old man wearing a woollen balaclava who said he was a pathologist, told how he had invested money in a collapsed pyramid scheme and called on the government to repay his losses.
A Kalashnikov assault rifle slung over one shoulder and a transistor radio over the other, he made his way into the trees after the other looters.
A burst of shooting was followed by a shout of pain and Will was lying on the ground with a bullet in his leg.
One of the soldiers who had earlier watched the looters steal their weapons washed Will's wound and bandaged it with a torn-up bed sheet. An Argentine journalist gave him a painkiller.

After a prolonged burst of fire over the barracks, which left Will and his rescuer flat on the parade ground as bullets crackled overhead, soldiers gathered up the half dozen rifles dropped by the fleeing looters and returned them to the arsenal.
